The hierarchy

Seven levels, from the atomic codepoint to the territory, all derived by bit-shifting.

  1. Territory — 16 zones (256 MiB)
  2. Zone — 16 districts (16 MiB)
  3. District — 16 planes (1 MiB)
  4. Plane — 65,536 codepoints
  5. Range — a declared allocation
  6. Block — a named run
  7. Codepoint — the atomic unit
Level Size Derived by Notes
Codepoint 1 — The atomic unit; e.g. 0x0011A000
Block variable named run Recorded in Blocks.txt
Range variable declared allocation Plugins declare ranges; collisions are rejected at boot
Plane 64 KiB CP >> 16 8192 planes (0x00–0x7FF)
District 16 planes CP >> 20 128 districts (0x00–0x7F)
Zone 16 districts CP >> 24 8 zones (0x00–0x07)
Territory 16 zones CP >> 28 8 territories (0x00–0x07)

The math

Address arithmetic makes the hierarchy total and cheap. Take the start of the BANcode registry, 0x0011A000:

SUCS_CP 0x0011A000
plane 0x0011 // System Control Plane
district 0x0011 >> 4 = 0x01
zone 0x0011 >> 8 = 0x00
territory 0x0011 >> 12 = 0x00
